newsitem.title: CHINA: Yanjing Brewery first-half net up 19.9 pc.
newsitem.headline: Yanjing Brewery first-half net up 19.9 pc.

text.p: Yanjing Brewery Co Ltd, China's biggest brewer, posted a 19.9 percent rise in first-half profits and linked the gains to higher turnover and improved sales of more profitable beers.

The company, which has a commanding 85 percent of the beer market in the nation's capital, reported net profits of 77.64 million yuan ($9.35 million) compared with 64.76 million in the year ago period.
Per-share net earnings reached 0.251 yuan in the first half, outperforming the company's target of 0.24 yuan for the period.
Sales hit 604.43 million yuan compared with 470.67 million yuan in the year-ago period, the company said in a report published in the China Securities newspaper.
It gave no details of the sales of its more profitable brands of beer but the company has been adding to production capacity and adjusting its product mix.
The Beijing-based brewer listed 72 million domestic A shares on the nation's southern bourse in Shenzhen last month.
Yanjing's officials have said the firm would use proceeds of 580 million yuan from the share issue to expand production capacity.
The company produced 363,733 tonnes of beer in the first half of this year, up 25.5 percent from the year-ago period, the report said.
The company would not announce a dividend.
Hong Kong-listed red chip Beijing Enterprises holds 54 percent of Yanjing while the brewer has a 6.9 percent stake in the corporate parent.
